course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 8

unit.title: Decimals
unit.blurb: Ordering decimals with inequality signs, multiplying and dividing by decimals, and mental strategies for decimal calculations.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Order and compare decimals, including negative decimals, using =, ≠, < and >.

O2.t: Multiply decimals by whole numbers and by other decimals.

O3.t: Divide whole numbers and decimals by a decimal.

O4.t: Use place value, factors and the laws of arithmetic to simplify decimal calculations.

p: Line the decimal points up and compare digits from the left. It can help to write zeros so every number has the same number of decimal places: 0.7 = 0.70 > 0.65.
For **negative** decimals, the one further from zero is smaller: −2.3 < −2.03.
**<** is less than, **>** is greater than, **≠** means 'is not equal to'. 4.50 = 4.5 but 4.05 ≠ 4.5.
0.125 is NOT bigger than 0.2 just because it has more digits: 0.125 < 0.200.
